claim_type_rationale: Single-master Wikipedia 'List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions' article supplies (a) the season-champion list defining the aggregation universe (76 seasons 1950-2025), (b) the pre-aggregated 'By driver' summary table providing Driver + Championship Count + Years-Won list per multi-champion driver, and (c) the ≥2-titles threshold cleanly splits the master's 'By driver' table into the 17 multi-champion partition vs the 18 single-time-champion partition. SQL: `SELECT driver, COUNT(*), MIN(year), MAX(year) FROM season_champions GROUP BY driver HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2`. The threshold ≥2 is a benchmark-curator-chosen cutoff but is anchored in the master's natural data shape — multi-champion vs single-time-champion is the canonical F1 historiographical distinction the master itself emphasizes via the 'By driver' summary. First Title Year + Last Title Year are MIN/MAX aggregates over the master's Years-Won column list (curator aggregation over source-supplied values; NOT separately sourced facts). source_count = 1 honestly reflects single-master sourcing.

collection_summary.approach: Cycle-0 source exploration: 3 sequential WebFetch passes against the master article's 'By driver' summary table. Pass 1 missed Lauda's 3rd title and Brabham's 3rd title (LLM summary errors). Pass 2 missed Ascari + Graham Hill entirely. Pass 3 with focused per-driver verification reconciled all 17 drivers. Universe locked at 17 drivers with ≥2 titles through 2025 season. Lando Norris winning 2025 (his 1st title) does NOT alter the ≥2-titles universe.

excluded_from_universe.single_time_champions_18_drivers: 18 drivers with exactly 1 World Drivers' Championship — out of scope per ≥2-titles threshold filter. The 18 (chronological by title year): Farina 1950, Hawthorn 1958, Phil Hill 1961, John Surtees 1964, Denny Hulme 1967, Jochen Rindt 1970 (posthumous), James Hunt 1976, Mario Andretti 1978, Jody Scheckter 1979, Alan Jones 1980, Keke Rosberg 1982, Nigel Mansell 1992, Damon Hill 1996, Jacques Villeneuve 1997, Kimi Räikkönen 2007, Jenson Button 2009, Nico Rosberg 2016, Lando Norris 2025. List reconciled to 18 names per cycle-1 audit verification (cycle-0 surfacing initially missed Nigel Mansell 1992 + Damon Hill 1996). Single-time-champion bucket arithmetic: 35 unique champions total − 17 multi-champion = 18 single-time, all enumerated here.

The cited master Wikipedia article's 'By driver' summary table is comprehensive for the 4-col schema; per-driver articles consulted only to verify ambiguous count claims surfaced during cycle-0 LLM-summary inconsistencies.

normalization_decisions.rule: Master Wikipedia article's visible-text driver name preserved verbatim including diacritic marks (Mika Häkkinen with umlaut over 'a'). No anglicization, no first-name truncation, no nickname substitution.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master uses canonical full names (Michael Schumacher, NOT 'Schumi'; Juan Manuel Fangio, NOT 'JM Fangio'; Mika Häkkinen with umlaut, NOT 'Hakkinen'). Verbatim preservation honors source_defined claim and matches Wikipedia's canonical biographical naming.

normalization_decisions.rule: Integer count of World Drivers' Championships per driver, matching master's 'By driver' summary table Titles column verbatim.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master pre-aggregates count per driver in the 'By driver' summary table. Verbatim integer; no curator counting beyond cross-checking against the master's Years-Won column entries per row.

normalization_decisions.field: First Title Year + Last Title Year
normalization_decisions.rule: First Title Year = MIN(year) over master's Years-Won column list per driver. Last Title Year = MAX(year) over the same list. Integer year only (master does not provide month/day granularity for season-championship dates).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master provides Years-Won as a comma-separated list per driver (e.g., Schumacher: 1994, 1995, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004). First/Last Title Year are computed MIN/MAX over this master-supplied list — curator aggregation over source values, not separately sourced facts. Documented as MIN/MAX aggregation in db_analog.

normalization_decisions.rule: HAVING-clause filter at Championship Count ≥ 2 separates 17 multi-champion drivers from 18 single-time champions in the master's 'By driver' table.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Threshold ≥2 is a benchmark-curator-chosen cutoff, but anchored in the master's natural categorical distinction between multi-champion and single-time-champion drivers. The cutoff is benchmark-explicit in the instance ID (`at_least_2`) and table_title and db_analog HAVING-clause. Alternative thresholds (≥3, ≥4) would yield smaller universes; ≥2 is the canonical 'multi-champion' boundary in F1 historiography.

normalization_decisions.rule: Championship Count DESC primary, First Title Year ASC secondary tiebreak. Chronological-first within count tier (e.g., 7-titles tier: Schumacher 1994 before Hamilton 2008; 4-titles tier: Prost 1985 before Vettel 2010 before Verstappen 2021).
normalization_decisions.rationale: Aggregation-table convention prioritizes count DESC (most-championed driver first). Within-tier tiebreak by First Title Year ASC produces chronological-first ordering — matches both Wikipedia 'By driver' table convention and natural reading order for F1 historiography (oldest-first within tier).

open_questions.question: Does Wikipedia's 'By driver' summary table use a different sort order (e.g., First Title Year ASC primary, ignoring count tiers)?
open_questions.resolution: Cycle-1 audit verified: source sort matches staged sort (Championship Count DESC primary + First Title Year ASC secondary tiebreak). No re-sort needed.

open_questions.question: Are there exactly 18 single-time F1 champions through 2025 season?
open_questions.resolution: Cycle-1 audit confirmed: exactly 18 single-time champions. Cycle-0 surfacing missed Nigel Mansell 1992 + Damon Hill 1996; cycle-2 repair updated excluded_from_universe.single_time_champions_18_drivers list to all 18 names (chronological by title year): Farina 1950, Hawthorn 1958, Phil Hill 1961, John Surtees 1964, Denny Hulme 1967, Jochen Rindt 1970, James Hunt 1976, Mario Andretti 1978, Jody Scheckter 1979, Alan Jones 1980, Keke Rosberg 1982, Nigel Mansell 1992, Damon Hill 1996, Jacques Villeneuve 1997, Kimi Räikkönen 2007, Jenson Button 2009, Nico Rosberg 2016, Lando Norris 2025. Arithmetic: 35 total − 17 multi = 18 single ✓.

open_questions.question: Should First Title Year + Last Title Year be staged as integers (current choice) or as full year-range strings (e.g., '1994-2004' for Schumacher)?
open_questions.resolution: Integer choice preserves numeric semantics for aggregation column_types. String-range would conflate MIN+MAX into a single text cell, losing the explicit MIN/MAX aggregation structure. Two-integer-column design is cleaner for db_analog SELECT MIN(...), MAX(...) and lets benchmark evaluators check each aggregate independently.

open_questions.question: Should the schema include nationality / constructor information per driver?
open_questions.resolution: No — 4-col aggregation-pure schema selected: Driver + Championship Count + First Title Year + Last Title Year. Adding Nationality or Constructor would either (a) over-specify beyond pure aggregation if from master, or (b) require per-driver article lookup inflating source_count. Nationality is mentioned in universe_listing.nationality for context but not staged as a column.

open_questions.question: How should Sort order handle the case where two drivers tie on both Championship Count AND First Title Year?
open_questions.resolution: No current tie exists in the 17-driver universe at both keys simultaneously. If a future tie emerges (e.g., two drivers winning their first title in the same season and the same total count), tertiary tiebreak via Last Title Year ASC or Driver-name alphabetical would resolve. Documented for future-proofing.

open_questions.question: What happens if Lando Norris wins a 2nd championship in 2026?
open_questions.resolution: Universe would extend from 17 to 18 drivers. Master article updates would propagate Norris from single-time to multi-time champion bucket. Benchmark instance temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this transition risk; re-staging would be needed when the master updates.

open_questions.question: How are championship years confirmed when a driver clinched mid-season vs end-of-season?
open_questions.resolution: Master uses season-year (calendar year of the F1 World Championship season), NOT clinch-date. E.g., Verstappen clinched 2021 title at the final race (Abu Dhabi, Dec 12 2021) but the season-year is 2021. Universe years staged per master's season-year convention.

decision_log.rationale: Single-master Wikipedia article + master's 'By driver' summary table = source-defined universe + values. Threshold ≥2 is benchmark-curator-chosen but anchored in master's natural categorical distinction. MIN/MAX year aggregates are curator aggregations over master-supplied year lists — NOT separately sourced. source_count = 1 honest.

decision_log.decision: Universe = 17 drivers with ≥2 F1 WDC titles through 2025 season
decision_log.rationale: Master article covers 76 seasons (1950-2025) with 35 unique champions; ≥2-titles threshold yields 17 multi-champion drivers. Lando Norris winning 2025 (first title) does not alter the ≥2 universe. Cycle-0 verification involved 3 sequential WebFetch passes to reconcile LLM-summary inconsistencies — pass 1 missed Lauda's 3rd + Brabham's 3rd; pass 2 missed Ascari + Graham Hill; pass 3 reconciled all 17. Audit should independently verify against the master.

Pure GROUP BY + COUNT/MIN/MAX + HAVING aggregation: `SELECT driver, COUNT(*), MIN(year), MAX(year) FROM seasons GROUP BY driver HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, MIN(year) ASC`. The HAVING-clause is part of aggregation semantics (post-aggregation filter on the COUNT aggregate), not a pre-aggregation row filter. operation_type vocab confirms 'aggregation' for COUNT/MIN/MAX/HAVING shape.

Matches operation_type = aggregation. The query asks 'how many championships per driver' (COUNT GROUP BY) + 'when did their championship-winning years start and end' (MIN/MAX aggregates), which is aggregation by definition. Floor lift brings aggregation from 5/5 to 6/5.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (Driver PK + Championship Count + First Title Year + Last Title Year)
decision_log.rationale: Pure aggregation-table shape: PK = grouping key (Driver), 1 COUNT aggregate (Championship Count), 2 MIN/MAX aggregates (First Title Year + Last Title Year). Excluded: title years list (multi-value cell), nationality (would require per-driver lookup or risk being a 5th data dimension beyond the aggregation pattern), constructor at title (changes between titles for many drivers — Lauda: Ferrari + McLaren; Senna: McLaren only; etc.; would over-specify). The 4-col selection prioritizes the cleanest aggregation pattern.
Driver name is unique in the master's 'By driver' summary table (master's grouping key). Single-key PK matches the GROUP BY semantics. Composite PK with Nationality or Years would be over-specified.

decision_log.decision: Sort = Championship Count DESC primary, First Title Year ASC secondary
decision_log.rationale: Aggregation-table convention: count DESC (most-championed driver first). Within-tier tiebreak by First Title Year ASC (chronological-first within tier). Yields ordering: Schumacher (7, 1994) → Hamilton (7, 2008) → Fangio (5, 1951) → Prost (4, 1985) → Vettel (4, 2010) → Verstappen (4, 2021) → Brabham (3, 1959) → Stewart (3, 1969) → Lauda (3, 1975) → Piquet (3, 1981) → Senna (3, 1988) → Ascari (2, 1952) → G. Hill (2, 1962) → Clark (2, 1963) → Fittipaldi (2, 1972) → Häkkinen (2, 1998) → Alonso (2, 2005).

F1 is the canonical Motorsport championship; Sports family per domain_taxonomy.md is the closest fit (joining Sports/Football, Sports/Olympics, Sports/Records precedents). 'Motorsport' subdomain captures the auto-racing specialization. Sports family extends from 4 subdomains (Football, Olympics, Records, ?) to +1.

decision_log.decision: Entity class = people/race-car-drivers (NEW fine-class within people bucket)
decision_log.rationale: F1 drivers are people; people bucket per pkdb_bench entity taxonomy. 'race-car-drivers' fine-class joins existing people/* fine-classes (astronauts, authors, judges, philosophers, physicists, mountaineers, monarchs, diplomats, presidents, justices, etc.). Floor lift adds +1 new fine-class to people bucket.

Universe shifts when a single-time champion wins a 2nd title (transition risk). Most recent transition: Verstappen 2022 (1→2 titles). Norris 2025 as new single-time champion does not transition. Future risk: Norris (or any current single-time champion still racing — Norris is the only one still active among single-timers since Räikkönen/Button/N.Rosberg are retired) could win in 2026+ extending the universe to 18. Decommissioning is impossible (titles don't get stripped retroactively under standard F1 rules). On benchmark timescales (1-3 years), universe expected to remain stable or grow by ≤1.

≥2 is the canonical 'multi-champion' threshold in F1 historiography (separates one-hit-wonders from repeat champions). ≥3 (yielding 11 drivers: 7,7,5,4×3,3×5) or ≥4 (yielding 6 drivers: 7,7,5,4×3) would yield smaller universes but lose the natural multi-vs-single distinction the master itself uses. ≥2 also satisfies benchmark preference for ≥10-row universes (17 ≥ 10).

cycle_0_design.approach: Source exploration via Wikipedia 'List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions' master article. Verified master's 'By driver' summary table provides pre-aggregated counts + year-lists per multi-champion driver supporting source-defined aggregation. Cross-checked universe size via 3 sequential WebFetch passes (pass 1 had recall errors on Lauda+Brabham 3rd titles + Clark's 2 titles; pass 2 missed Ascari + Graham Hill; pass 3 with focused per-driver verification reconciled all 17 drivers). Selected the 17-row ≥2-titles universe. Designed 4-col aggregation-pure schema (Driver PK + Championship Count + First Title Year + Last Title Year) avoiding nationality/constructor over-specification.
cycle_0_design.outcome: Staged 4-column schema with 17-row CSV. aggregation category + aggregation operation_type + source_defined claim_type + Sports/Motorsport domain (NEW subdomain) + people/race-car-drivers entity class (NEW fine-class). Includes normalization_decisions (5 entries) + open_questions (7 entries) from cycle-0 per cycle-2 lesson from antarctic-stations: these required curation fields must be staged upfront, not added in cycle-2 repair.
